Assistant: Done — all open PRs reviewed and merged. There was only one across both repos:

**NMP #2940** (codex's browser-runtime RC publish-graph fix) — merged. It's the fix that unblocks the stalled crates.io `nmp-browser-runtime@1.0.0-rc.1` publish: the crate was importing repost-kind constants that don't exist in the already-published, immutable `nmp-kinds@1.0.0-rc.1`, so it now derives them from `nostr::Kind` instead. Clean (+14/-8), behavior-preserving, no concept-dep added, `cargo publish --dry-run` validated, all 16 CI checks green. I filed **#3015** as a p3 follow-up to return that derivation to `nmp-kinds` on the next release (so the release-graph workaround doesn't quietly violate single-source-of-truth permanently).

All Chirp PRs from this session's work are already merged (the whole validation wave: #49/#52/#55/#56/#57/#58/#59). So the tracker is clean — zero open PRs in either repo.

Notably, merging #2940 means the crates.io rc.1 publish is now unblocked on the code side — if you want, the remaining step there is codex (or me) actually running the `cargo publish` for `nmp-browser-runtime` and the crates after it in the graph. That, plus the P2 validation sweep, are the two open threads. Want me to drive the crates.io publish to completion now that its blocker is merged, or hold?
